reason: the operating system stops a read part way only when the device under the file goes away during it (a network share dropping, a disk failing); no file a test can write locally is read that way
output() writes to the standard output of the process that calls it, which the test harness holds open; the crate ships no program a test could start with a closed standard output
standard output refuses a write only behind a full disk or a vanished device, and the test harness holds its own standard output open on neither
every catalogue value reaches the Rust module as a JSON-quoted string literal, so only a defect in a renderer under codegen/ makes rustfmt refuse the module; no catalogue input provokes it
a command raises a cause no part declares only through a defect in this repository's own command code; no input, file or state provokes it
getrandom fails only when the kernel's random source is unavailable (no getentropy, no /dev/urandom), which no unprivileged test can arrange on a running machine
Telemetry::ask reads only when stdin and stderr are terminals, and a terminal refuses a read only when its device goes away mid-read; a test process has no terminal to take away
